question: Does rehearsing a skill only in your head, without moving, improve how you later perform it?
options: Yes, but less than real practice
Yes, as much as real practice
answer: Yes, but less than real practice. Driskell, Copper and Moran pooled dozens of studies and found mental rehearsal improved performance, more for tasks heavy in thinking, such as planning a sequence, than for strength or stamina. The benefit faded unless renewed. A pianist can rehearse fingering on a train; the train cannot replace the keys.
move: When you cannot practise, rehearse in your head, then test it for real.
ask: Which skill could I rehearse in my head during dead time this week?
trap: Without movement, it seems nothing can be trained.
source: Driskell, Copper and Moran, J. Applied Psychology, 1994
reference: Driskell, Copper and Moran, Does mental practice enhance performance?, Journal of Applied Psychology, 1994
